F-C1.title: Certificates: expiring and forged certificates are alerts and are refused

F-C2.title: Configuration: a policy or data set that drifted from what was generated is caught

F-D1.title: Storage: the database volume is lost - restored from an encrypted backup with data, control and audit integrity

F-D2.title: Storage: the database is unavailable during a load

F-D3.title: Storage: retention overdue and storage pressure are alerts

F-E1.title: Edge: the process is killed mid-stream and starts again on its outbox

F-E2.title: Edge: the model is missing, tampered or failing - the runtime says so and the baseline serves

F-E3.title: Edge: input is bad - invalid, duplicate, out of order, stale or unsynchronised

F-M1.title: Model: a rotted active model is detected and rolled back to the previous verified version

F-M2.title: Model: a tampered package is refused at load and at activation

F-M3.title: Model: input to a forecast is stale or has a gap - the service abstains

F-N1.title: Network: the uplink is lost (the broker stopped) and restored

F-N2.title: Network: the identity provider is unreachable

F-N3.title: Network: a workload reaches what it should not (a broken isolation)

F-P1.title: Policy: the engine is unreachable - every protected request is refused, an approved command is held, nothing is waved through

F-P2.title: Policy: the engine answers nothing, garbage or a loosely typed permit - treated as unavailable

F-P3.title: Policy: what the engine enforces is what was reviewed (thousands of generated contexts against the reference)

F-S1.title: Stream: Kafka is unavailable while events keep arriving

F-S2.title: Stream: events are replayed or duplicated, and content conflicts

F-S3.title: Stream: invalid events are refused at the gateway and never reach Kafka

F-V1.title: Service: each component is restarted (database, Kafka, broker, identity, gateway, API, ingestion, policy engine)

F-V2.title: Service: a worker is killed mid-action - the action is not repeated and the request is closed as abandoned

F-V3.title: Service: a crashed edge runtime is detected, becomes one incident, is restarted once and resolves

F-V4.title: Service: a fault that cannot be repaired is escalated to a person and automation stands down

F-V5.title: Service: a bad rollout of the API and of a worker

F-V6.title: Service: the command executor is killed while a command is executing - the orphan is reconciled before anything new runs and is never driven again

F-X1.title: SAFE-02: a protected action that lacks evidence, a valid decision or fresh state is denied and never executed (every adapter, every way)

F-X2.title: SAFE-03: stale state fails safe in every consumer (state service, KPI record, forecast, routing, recommendation, command policy)

notes.recovery_objectives_are_measured_not_ass: P11.05: RTO and RPO measured on the target (see the evidence's metrics)
notes.what_this_is: each fault class of the acceptance (edge, network, stream, service, model, policy, storage) with the evidence that the fault was induced and what the platform did; two labs written for this phase (SAFE-02, SAFE-03, REC-01) and the target and lab evidence of Phases 05-11
